findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Build the G4-only and both-criteria attribution cases as hand-built Pass-1 outputs passed straight to `score("attributes_g3_vs_g4", ...)` (not through `run_case("plan-review-G3")`, which drops out-of-set criteria), and add a G4 case scored against the both-criteria finding.
evidence: Plan: "G3 must-fire case with output from `passes.pass1_container` shape (built through `eval_solver.run_case("plan-review-G3", ...)`) credited to G3; a G4-only finding on a G3 case fails; a finding with `criteria: ["G3", "G4"]` is credited."
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:379-381 — `crit = [c for c in (f.get("criteria") or []) if c in valid_ids]; if not crit: continue`
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:130-137 — `pass1_container(..., criteria=[desc], ...)` passes the single evaluated criterion
findings.finding: The attribution tests for 'G4-only finding on a G3 case fails' and 'criteria: ["G3", "G4"] is credited' don't say how their output is built. The only route the plan names is `eval_solver.run_case("plan-review-G3", ...)`, which calls `pass1_container` with `criteria=[desc]` for G3 alone, and that drops out-of-set tags (`passes.py:379-381`). Built that way, the G4-only finding is removed before scoring, so the case fails because there are no findings, not because attribution was rejected. The test would pass even without the new `criteria`-list logic. The both-criteria finding would also reach the scorer as `["G3"]` only, so the 'credited to each' behaviour would never be exercised.
findings.location: Testing → attribution bullet; AC 3 (`attributes_g3_vs_g4` ... credits a both-criteria finding, and rejects the wrong criterion)
scenarios: An implementer builds all three attribution cases through `run_case("plan-review-G3")`. The G4-only finding is filtered out upstream and the 'rejects wrong criterion' test passes against unchanged code.
The both-criteria finding reaches the scorer as `criteria: ["G3"]`, so the claim that it is credited to each of G3 and G4 is never tested.
findings.suggested_fix: In Testing, say: 'the G4-only and `["G3","G4"]` cases are hand-built `{"findings": [{"finding": "x", "criteria": [...]}]}` outputs scored directly; the both-criteria finding is scored against both a G3 and a G4 must-fire case and passes each; also a `G33`-only finding on a G3 case fails.'

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:379-381: `crit = [c for c in (f.get("criteria") or []) if c in valid_ids]; if not crit: continue`
The plan's own Root cause section says findings with no in-set criterion are dropped, but the Testing section does not carry that rule over to the attribution tests
findings.finding: For the attribution tests 'a G4-only finding on a G3 case fails' and 'a finding with criteria ["G3","G4"] is credited', the plan never says whether the scorer input is built through `run_case("plan-review-G3", ...)` (the path it names for the first attribution test) or written by hand. Through `run_case`, `pass1_container` runs with `criteria=[desc]` (G3 only) and drops every criterion outside that set. So the G4-only finding never reaches `_attributes_criterion`: the test fails on 'no findings' rather than on wrong attribution. The both-criteria finding arrives as `["G3"]`, so the 'credited to each' rule is never tested.
findings.location: Testing — attribution bullet; AC 3 (`attributes_g3_vs_g4` credits ... a both-criteria finding, and rejects the wrong criterion)
scenarios: A test author reuses the `run_case("plan-review-G3")` harness for all three attribution tests. The G4-only test passes even if the new `criteria` branch credits any criterion, and the both-criteria test passes even if the code only checks `criteria[0]`.
findings.suggested_fix: In Testing, change the attribution bullet to: keep the `run_case("plan-review-G3", ...)` positive test. Then add direct scorer calls on hand-built `{"findings": [{"finding": "x", "criteria": [...]}]}` outputs: `["G4"]` on a G3 case fails; `["G3","G4"]` passes on both a G3 case and a G4 case; `["G33"]` on a G3 case fails.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add attribution unit tests asserting that a finding with `criteria: ["G33"]` is NOT credited on a G3 case and that `criteria: ["g3"]` IS credited.
evidence: "by exact case-insensitive element match (so `G3` never matches `G33`)"
Testing attribution bullet lists only: G3 credited, G4-only fails, ["G3","G4"] credited
AC: "credits attribution carried in a finding's `criteria` list by exact element match ... checked by unit tests"
findings.finding: The attribution change promises two properties that no planned test checks. It says matching is an exact element match ('so `G3` never matches `G33`') and that it is case-insensitive. The Testing section covers only three cases: a correct G3 finding, a G4-only finding, and a finding listing both G3 and G4. There is no near-miss case (a `G33` finding on a G3 case) and no case-variant case (`g3`). A naive substring or case-sensitive implementation would therefore pass every planned test, even though the AC claims 'exact element match ... checked by unit tests'.
findings.location: Testing — attribution bullet; Approach step 3; AC 3
scenarios: An implementation that matches `criterion in str(criteria)` passes all planned tests but credits a G33 finding to G3.
A case-sensitive `==` passes all planned tests but scores a model-emitted `g3` as unattributed.
findings.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_eval_scorers.py, add two parametrized cases to the attribution test: `criteria: ["G33"]` on a G3 case expects passed=False, and `criteria: ["g3"]` on a G3 case expects passed=True.

findings.finding: The fresh-interpreter test that proves the scorer 'registers the contract itself' never asserts its precondition that `rebar.llm.plan_review.passes` has not been imported. If importing `eval_scorers` already pulls in `passes` transitively (e.g. via eval_solver or findings), the test passes without the in-function `register_contracts()` call doing anything.
findings.location: Testing — 'called on a hand-built Pass-1 output in a fresh interpreter ... that never imported `passes`'; AC 2
scenarios: eval_scorers or an import it makes imports passes at module load, so the registration path is never exercised but the test is green.

A pass also proves no review_result fallback, because that model would reject the output for missing `dimension`.

findings.finding: The plan's list of what consumes the `emits_valid_findings` scorer name covers only the seven packaged criterion-id specs and the three PASS specs. These are all criterion-id specs that resolve through `_criterion_id` (including dotted `project.*` ids) and emit the Pass-1 shape.
